notice: SAMPLE DATA. No live feed is wired. These items are invented for the game's own fictional Melbourne and are attributed to invented outlets on purpose — putting made-up headlines under a real masthead would be a fake news feed, which is worse than an honest empty one. This file is a POOL: the board draws six of them for the day, deterministically, so the square is not the same board every morning. Replace this file by running: node mvp/scripts/townsquare-refresh-news.mjs --live (see that script's header for the key, host and cadence the owner must supply first).

items.headline: Cash rate held again; four of nine economists now expect a cut before Christmas
items.summary: The board left the rate where it was for a fourth meeting and said very little about the fifth. Fixed-rate expiries continue to roll through the inner north.

items.headline: Half the fixed book written in the boom rolls off this year, and it rolls off at today's rate
items.summary: Lenders are writing to borrowers earlier than they used to. Two have moved their hardship teams onto the same floor as retentions.

items.headline: Serviceability buffer stays at three points; brokers report deals failing on the stress test alone
items.summary: Applications that clear on income are falling over on the assessment rate. Nobody wants to be the first to argue about the buffer in public.

items.headline: Fitzroy North objection period closes with fourteen pages from the residents' association
items.summary: Two towers on the corridor advanced to hearing. A third was sent back over overshadowing of a laneway that the applicant describes as a service lane and the objectors describe as a street.

items.headline: Shadow diagrams requested a second time on an application already twenty weeks old
items.summary: The applicant supplied the diagrams in week one at a different scale. The clock does not stop while the scale is argued about.

items.headline: Permit issued on the corner site; the vendor lists it the following Tuesday
items.summary: Eleven months of process, and the site changed hands before a shovel touched it. The buyer is described in the contract as a nominee.

items.headline: Structural timber up again; suppliers move to seven-day quote validity
items.summary: Merchants report quotes expiring before they are accepted. Steel is flat. Concrete is flat and everyone is suspicious about it.

items.headline: Variations now average nine per cent of contract value on inner-city renovations
items.summary: Builders say the number is honest and clients say it is a second contract. Both are describing the same spreadsheet.

items.headline: Formwork crews booked out to the end of the quarter; two sites stood down waiting
items.summary: A concrete pour that misses its crew does not simply move. It moves everything behind it, and the crane hire keeps invoicing.

items.headline: Clearance rate 68 per cent on 612 reported auctions; three inner-north sales above reserve by more than 20 per cent
items.summary: Volumes are up on the same weekend last year. Passed-in stock is being negotiated within the week rather than relisted.

items.headline: A fifth of Saturday's passed-in stock is under contract by Tuesday afternoon
items.summary: The board reports Saturday. The money reports Tuesday. Only one of those two numbers gets printed on Sunday.

items.headline: Quoted ranges drift within reach of the result for a third consecutive weekend
items.summary: Agents describe this as a return to discipline. Vendors describe it as a soft market. The ranges themselves are simply less wrong than usual.

items.headline: Heritage overlay extended over two more streets; six pending applications caught
items.summary: The extension was recommended by the council's own consultant and opposed by every applicant it touches. One of them has owned the site for eleven days.

items.headline: Facade retention approved on the bank building; the rear is consented for demolition
items.summary: What is being kept is a wall and a parapet. What is being lost is the banking chamber, which is the only part anyone ever photographed.

items.headline: Bluestone cellar found under a slab in Richmond halts works for three weeks
items.summary: The stone was catalogued, lifted and sold. The report notes that this outcome is both legal and slightly sad.

items.headline: Tram route extension confirmed to the northern end of the corridor, works from next quarter
items.summary: Stops move, one is removed, and the affected block loses kerbside parking for three quarters. Frontages along the route are already being quietly assembled.

items.headline: Kerbside parking removed on two blocks; traders petition, then reprice
items.summary: Footfall counts published a quarter later show the traders were right about the fortnight and wrong about the year.

items.headline: The stop being removed serves more people than the two being added, according to the objectors' own count
items.summary: The department has not disputed the count. It has disputed what the count means, which is a longer argument.

items.headline: Listing volumes up eleven per cent; credit growth flat for the third month
items.summary: One of those two numbers is describing intent and the other is describing capacity. They have not agreed since March.

items.headline: Advertised rents flat in the inner north for the first quarter in two years
items.summary: Vacancy is unchanged. What has changed is how long a listing sits before the price on it changes.

items.headline: Commercial yields widen a quarter point; three funds mark their books and one does not
items.summary: The fund that did not mark its book has the most confident newsletter of the three.

items.headline: Tribunal list runs eight months; applicants begin costing the wait into the offer
items.summary: A site with a permit and a site with a hearing date are now two different assets with two different buyers.

items.headline: Waterproofing tops the defect list again; the same three details account for most of it
items.summary: None of the three details is difficult. All three are the first thing removed when a job is value-engineered.

items.headline: A result twenty per cent above reserve tells you about the reserve
items.summary: The valuer's file, obtained by nobody, would say the same thing in less interesting language.
